text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. President Bill Clinton: Talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will focus on Syrian track.
- Netanyahu may visit King Hassan of Morocco on return from Washington next month.
- Israeli industrial production up 5 percent in November.
- Central bank denies plan to abandon exchange rate system. Finance Minister Dan Meridor: Treasury opposes changes in diagonal mechanism.

- Northern Telecom buys 20 percent stake in Telrad telecommunication and electronic industries, subsidiary of Koor Industries, for $45 million through Nortel Communications, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary.
- Shamrock group interested in buying Bank Hapoalim's shares in Koor Industries.

- Quantum Industrial Holdings, a fund managed by financier George Soros's Soros Fund Management LLC, and Comverse Technology announce formation of new private equity fund that will focus on investing in Israeli high tech companies.
- Prime Minister's deputy director-general Moshe Leon strongly rejects suggestions there will be job losses as a result of government's newly announced privatisation programme.
GLOBES
- Meridor: Exchange rate system won't be changed. It's possible to change the interest rate also once a day.
- National council for planning approves Ben-Gurion Airport 2000 project.
- Dead Sea Works and Volkswagen in negotiations to sell 25 percent of magnesium foundry factory to Austrian Unitech company.
MAARIV
- Army examined possibilities for defending northern Israel -- without parts of the Golan. The examination was on orders of Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai ahead of resumed talks with Syria.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Body of one of Waxman's murderers will be transferred to Palestinians today.
- Bitter confrontation between Treasury and Bank of Israel on change in exchange rate.
- El Al workers searching for partner to buy control of airline.
- Knesset mobilizes public relations firm to improve image.
HAARETZ
- 84 more settlements added to map of national preference to be brought before government for approval in coming days. These include Emmanuel, Kiryat Arba and others in Hebron area.
- Greek and Israeli navies to conduct joint maneouvres this summer in Aegean Sea, says Greek ambassador to Israel.
- Prime minister tells Haaretz: It's possible to renew negotiations with Syria on basis of disagreement.
